clue.text: PM's about done, so stay the night

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the noun, an overnight stay at someone's home

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the prime minister's name is read backwards

parts.note: Sir Robert Peel was a British Prime Minister; PM's gives PEEL'S, written PEELS
done, as in finished, means over

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister, his business finished, decides to stay overnight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the PM's name; Robert Peel was a 19th-century British Prime Minister. The definition is loose: a verb phrase for the noun naming an overnight stay.
explanation.definitionFit: A night spent as a guest at a friend's house is the event itself, so staying the night describes it loosely.

clue.text: Fish spawn covers river

indicators.note: covers means surrounds, so one piece goes outside the other

parts.note: spat is the spawn of oysters or other shellfish

explanation.surface: Fish eggs blanket a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprat is a small fish of the herring family.

clue.text: Point to curved entrance, not right for a place at least

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point

indicators.note: not means without, so a letter is removed

parts.note: an archway is an entrance under an arch

explanation.surface: Someone directs us to an arched doorway that is not on the right side.
explanation.walkthrough: An each-way bet in British racing pays out if the horse wins or is placed, finishing in the top few.
explanation.definitionFit: A bet backing a horse to win or finish in the top places pays out at least for a place.

clue.text: Worth canvassing bore, needing somewhere to 'eat

parts.note: a pain is a tiresome person, a bore
a table is where you eat, with the h dropped in Cockney style

explanation.surface: A dull person, worth campaigning to, wants a place to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canvassing' looks like seeking votes but means painting on canvas; the dropped h of 'eat is only colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worth putting on canvas is fit to be painted.

clue.text: In wandering life, see African country? Saw round it

parts.note: V is short for vide, Latin for see

indicators.note: round it says the saying goes around the country just named

parts.note: a saw is an old saying, an adage
Gabon is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: A wanderer is told to look at an African nation and cut around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a verb or tool but is a proverb; 'round it' wraps the saying around the country just named.
explanation.definitionFit: Vagabondage is the condition of being a vagabond, a life of wandering.

clue.text: Grass twisted by ear

indicators.note: by ear means as heard, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: wry means twisted or contorted

explanation.surface: Grass bent over by the ear of a crop.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is a cereal grass grown for grain.

clue.text: I'm accepted in Basle, having managed to break into football team

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: FC stands for Football Club
managed, as in ran a business, gives ran

explanation.surface: Someone welcomed in a Swiss city has also managed to get into a football side.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks as the currency itself: the Swiss coin is accepted in Basle, a city in Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swiss currency unit is legal tender in Basle, so it can say it is accepted there.

clue.text: From miles away, grasp spoken language

parts.note: far means a long way off

indicators.note: spoken says the word is to be taken as said, not written

parts.note: to see a point is to grasp it

explanation.surface: Understanding a language spoken from far away.
explanation.definitionFit: Farsi is the Persian language of Iran.

clue.text: God! Are you ambassador? Not half

parts.note: thou art is the old form of you are

indicators.note: not half means only half is used, the first four of eight letters

parts.note: an ambassador is an emissary

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise on asking whether someone is an envoy, answered with emphasis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' looks like the British slang for 'very much' but keeps half of EMISSARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemis is the Greek goddess of hunting, a deity.

clue.text: Objection: being obedient, I must step down

indicators.note: stepping down moves the letter lower in this down entry

parts.note: being obedient is being compliant

explanation.surface: Someone protests that, being docile, they must resign.
explanation.walkthrough: In COMPLIANT the I moves down one place to make COMPLAINT.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint is an expression of objection or grievance.

clue.text: Police chief trying to get on the ball?

definitions.text: trying to get on the ball?

parts.note: RUC was the Royal Ulster Constabulary, the police force of Northern Ireland
a king is a chief or ruler

explanation.surface: A senior police officer is attempting to stay alert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Police chief' reads as one officer but splits in two. In rugby a ruck is a scrum formed over the ball on the ground, which players contest to win it.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby, rucking is the contest of forwards over a loose ball, each side driving to win possession of it.

clue.text: Signs of hesitation about vermin a mistake

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the hesitation sounds go round the pest

parts.note: er and um are both noises of hesitation
a rat is vermin

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates, umming and erring, over pests and admits a slip.
explanation.definitionFit: An erratum is an error in print, so it is a mistake corrected in a list of errata.

clue.text: That is what to do with broken-down car

definitions.meaning: a formal way of saying namely, introducing a clarification

definitions.text: what to do with broken-down car
definitions.meaning: a car that will not go has to be pulled by a truck, read as the instruction 'haul it'

explanation.surface: Explaining exactly what you must do with a car that has broken down.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words, the answer reads as an instruction to pull the car away.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin-derived phrase means namely, and split in two it is also a command to haul the car away.

clue.text: Such ceremony — it is to get boy shortly on to roll

parts.note: a bap is a soft bread roll in Britain
'tis is the old contraction of it is
Mal is a shortened form of the boy's name Malcolm

explanation.surface: A ceremony where a young boy is given a bread roll.
explanation.walkthrough: A bap is a British soft bread roll; 'on to' says the other pieces follow the roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A christening is a baptism, and the adjective describes anything belonging to that ceremony.

clue.text: Ask people's views about one requirement for plant

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the phrase goes round the numeral

parts.note: to poll the nation is to ask the people's opinions
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A survey of opinion about one thing a plant needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowering plants need pollen transferred between flowers to set seed.

clue.text: Commander finds girls' gang very short

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the abbreviation is taken out

parts.note: a bevy is a group, especially of girls or women

explanation.surface: A commander discovers that a group of girls is greatly under strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very short' looks like a description of the gang but means lacking V for very.
explanation.definitionFit: A bey was a governor or military commander in the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: What's needed to travel in the wild: vehicle, horse, and boat

definitions.text: What's needed to travel in the wild

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle
H is slang for heroin, itself called horse
a craft is a boat

explanation.surface: A list of transport needed for a wilderness journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' is slang for heroin, which is abbreviated H.
explanation.definitionFit: Bushcraft is the skill of surviving and finding your way in wild country.

clue.text: Not allow gaps in the trees? Hard one for Asian

parts.note: to ban something is to not allow it
glades are open spaces in a wood
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Forbidding clearings in a forest seems hard on someone from Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Bangladesh in South Asia is an Asian.

clue.text: No heart to drive vehicle — he runs people down

indicators.note: no heart means the middle letters are taken out

parts.note: a tractor is a farm vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone without the spirit to drive a vehicle who criticises others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No heart' empties DRIVE to DE. 'runs down' looks like a road accident but means belittles.
explanation.definitionFit: A detractor disparages others, running them down in speech.

clue.text: Create a stir, reorganising office

indicators.note: reorganising signals the letters of the phrase being arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A shake-up of an office causes a fuss among the staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A secretariat is an administrative office or department, as of the United Nations.

clue.text: Turn up outside place for work out

indicators.note: outside means going around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: to turn up is to come
to place something is to put it

explanation.surface: Arriving outside a workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: To compute is to calculate, to work out a figure.

clue.text: Part of body with painful disease? Nothing to be removed

indicators.note: to be removed says one piece comes out of the other

parts.note: gout is a painful disease of the joints
O, the figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A question about which body part is affected by a disease, with nothing needing surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: The gut is the intestine, a part of the body.

clue.text: Away by train, not first-class: her sister chose Cornwall

parts.note: gone means away

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter goes

parts.note: rail is travel by train
A, as in A1, means first-class

explanation.surface: A woman leaves by second-class rail while her sister married into Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: In King Lear, Goneril's sister Regan is married to the Duke of Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: Goneril is a daughter of Shakespeare's King Lear, sister of Regan, wife of the Duke of Cornwall.

clue.text: In our time, area used by one with grazing rights

parts.note: in England a commoner is someone entitled to graze animals on common land

explanation.surface: In the present day a piece of land is used by someone allowed to graze animals.
explanation.walkthrough: Commoners in England hold traditional rights to graze livestock on shared common land.
explanation.definitionFit: Common Era is the secular name for the era counted from year one, the period in which we live.

clue.text: Had died at sea, but for doctor

indicators.note: but for means except, so the letters are left out

parts.note: drowned means died in water

explanation.surface: Someone would have drowned at sea had there been no doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Owned and had both mean possessed, as in 'had a house'.

clue.text: Bug has some leg caught and twisted

indicators.note: caught means held, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: some means any, as in 'have you any?'

indicators.note: twisted means turned round, so the cricket word is read backwards

parts.note: on is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: An insect has a leg trapped and bent.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is also called the on side; 'twisted' reverses it and 'caught' holds it inside the word for some.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug someone is to irritate them, a colloquial verb sense.

clue.text: Delicious curry finally covers top of stomach

indicators.note: covers the top means takes the place of the first letter

parts.note: tummy is a child's word for stomach

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A tasty curry ends up filling the stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: The Y from 'curry finally' replaces the T at the top of TUMMY.
explanation.definitionFit: Yummy is a colloquial word for tasty or delicious.

clue.text: Graduate snipping end off a wart — star turn

indicators.note: cutting off the end means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a wart is a lump on the skin

indicators.note: turn means turned round, so the star is read backwards

parts.note: the Sun is a star

explanation.surface: A graduate who has a wart removed is the star performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snipping end off' cuts LUMP to LUM; 'turn' makes SUN into NUS.
explanation.definitionFit: An alumnus is a former student or graduate of a school or university.

clue.text: Fail to retain interest in endless tale

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a saga is a long tale

explanation.surface: A long story that bores its audience.
explanation.definitionFit: To sag is to flag or droop, as interest does when it is not held.

clue.text: Provisional, almost meriting being redone

indicators.note: redone means made again, so the letters are reassembled
almost means the last letter is left off the word

explanation.surface: Something temporary nearly earns a second attempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims MERITING to MERITIN, which 'being redone' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Interim describes a temporary arrangement, standing until something permanent replaces it.

clue.text: Last to groove in jazz dance

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the letter goes within the jazz word

parts.note: trad is traditional jazz

indicators.note: last to means the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Finally getting into the groove at a jazz dance.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAD is British shorthand for traditional jazz.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread a measure is an old way of saying to dance, so the verb can mean dance.

clue.text: In anger, yell horribly most of the time

indicators.note: horribly suggests the words are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shouts angrily and dreadfully, most of the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Generally means usually or as a rule, that is on most occasions.
